I have some experience with this type of technology so I had an advantage.There is know doubt that as with all technology you get what you pay for and a little reading up on the subject won't hurt. Important with this type of system is knowing that you will still get something from your investment when the days are not at all sunny. A solar inverter requires a level of input voltage before it will start producing electricity. Smaller less efficient systems will struggle on less favourable days.Most of the representatives made the experience more akin to buying a car including that old favourite of calling the manager to cut a special deal. They mostly had two offers, inexpensive blockbuster and quality (normal) equipment and were mostly unwilling to provide anything outside of their current offers. If they did, the prices were inflated.In the end I chose a local company who knew what they were talking about and were willing to make changes based on my needs and wants, without overly inflating the costs. I am happy with my purchase and am confident that Solar Connections will provide ongoing support should I need it.
